messages.subject: Latent interaction problems (indProd,SEM,probe2WayMC)
parts:
Hi there,
I'm trying to model a latent interaction in a SEM using the WLSMV due to categorical indicators on my outcome variables (I & E). The interaction is between age (observed variable) and three latent constructs. Therefore, I'm using the indProd-package to calculate the respective product-terms.
The model terminates normally without any error. When I try to probe my interaction using the probe2WayMC function, I'm getting the following error: 

Error in est$beta[nameY,nameX]: subscript out of bounds.

This is my syntax:

dat<- indProd(dat,
              c("age"),
              c("NoSKMSM" , "KSMChrMX" , "KSMSMx",
                "NoSN"  , "NChrMX" , "NSMx",
                "NoSEMnew", "EMChrMX"  , "EMSMX"),
              residualC=T,
              match=F,
              names=c("age_anos","age_achr","age_as",
                      "age_nnos","age_nchr","age_ns",
                      "age_enos","age_echr","age_es"))

mod <- '
  
#Latente Faktoren
                 
                 A   =~ NoSKMSM  + KSMChrMX + KSMSMx
                 N   =~ NoSN   + NChrMX + NSMx 
                 EM  =~ NoSEMnew + EMChrMX  + EMSMX
                 I   =~ D_VORH + A_VORH + AIMAX  
                 E   =~ O_VORH + C_VORH  + AD_MAX   

#Latente Ieraktionen

                 Mod_A_age =~ age_anos + age_as + age_achr
                 Mod_N_age =~ age_nnos + age_ns + age_nchr
                 Mod_em_age =~ age_enos + age_es + age_echr

                 Mod_A_age ~  0*age
                 Mod_A_age ~~ 0*A
                 Mod_N_age ~  0*age
                 Mod_N_age ~~ 0*N
                 Mod_em_age ~  0*age
                 Mod_em_age ~~ 0*EM

################################################## Regressionen
                 
                 I ~ A + N + EM + age + sex +  Mod_A_age + Mod_N_age + Mod_em_age
                 E ~ A + N + EM + age + sex +  Mod_A_age + Mod_N_age + Mod_em_age 
                 
################################################## latente Korrelationen
                 
                 A ~~ EM + N 
                 # A ~ KB
                 N ~~ EM 
                 # N ~ KB
                 # EM  ~ KB
                 I ~~ E
                  '

sem2_mod <- sem(mod, 
                data=dat,
                estimator = "WLSMV",
                mimic="Mplus",
                start="Mplus",
                meanstructure = T,
                ordered = c("D_VORH",
                            "A_VORH",
                            "AIMAX",
                            "O_VORH",  
                            "C_VORH",
                            "AD_MAX"))

summary(sem2_mod, 
        fit.measures = TRUE,  
        standardize  = TRUE, 
        rsquare      = TRUE, 
        estimates    = TRUE, 
        ci           = FALSE)

probe2WayMC(sem2_mod,
            nameX = c("age", "A" , "N" , "EM" ,"sex","KB", "Mod_A_age", "Mod_N_age",
            "Mod_em_age"),
            nameY = "I",
            modVar = "age",
            valProbe= c(4,16))

Any hints on how to solve the problem are highly appreciated. I'm also not sure if I should use the probe2WayMC or RC-function. I'm guessing, if I select ResidualC=T in the indProd-function, RC would be appropriate. However, that gives me a similar error regarding the est$psi.
Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Latent interaction problems (indProd,SEM,probe2WayMC)
parts: I'm trying to model a latent interaction in a SEM using the WLSMV due to categorical indicators on my outcome variables (I & E). The interaction is between age (observed variable) and three latent constructs. Therefore, I'm using the indProd-package to calculate the respective product-terms.

Product indicators are only appropriate for continuous indicators.  There is not a "product" of 2 categories.

Here is a recent paper that compared some methods for categorical indicators.  

https://doi.org/10.1177%2F0013164419865017

With only 3 indicators per factor, their recommended parceling strategy is not an option.  If you have at least 5 categories, I expect you could get away with simply treating the items as continuous, in which case you could use product indicators as you intended.
I'm also not sure if I should use the probe2WayMC or RC-function. I'm guessing, if I select ResidualC=T in the indProd-function, RC would be appropriate.
Error in est$beta[nameY,nameX]: subscript out of bounds.

I expect the problem is that the function expects the first-order effects to be latent variable names as well.  You have interactions of latent variables with age, which is observed.  I would recommend treating it like a single-indicator construct (which is what lavaan does internally without telling you, to save you the trouble):  

AGE =~ age
age ~~ 0*age

Then use AGE in the rest of your syntax in place of age.

But also make sure you are using the latest development version of the package, just in case this was an old bug that was already resolved.  In a fresh R session, run:

devtools::install_github("simsem/semTools/semTools")

Then restart R before running your script.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Dear Terrence,

thanks a lot for the helpful suggestions! 
I guess I did not point out one important detail: My indicators are continuous, my outcome variables are not. Thus, I thought the product-indicator approach should work.

The advise you gave regarding the age-variable seems to be working. Additionally, I did play around a bit and realized, that the probe2WayMC-function works by only entering the variables that are part of the interaction. Thus, I threw out all the other independent variables and probed each interaction individually. I would be very happy for another hint if that approach is not feasible in your eyes.
